match.reason: The bank's SWOT analysis point covers only SWOT at a Year 11 level, while the new point is broader, combining SWOT with the product life cycle for Year 12 situational analysis, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Situational analysis
card: Situational analysis is the first step in the marketing process. The business looks at where it stands now, before it sets goals or plans.
Strengths and weaknesses are internal, so the business can control them. Opportunities and threats are external, such as a rival opening nearby or a change in customer tastes.
Each product moves through stages: introduction, growth, maturity and decline. Sales and profit differ at each stage, so the stage shows what the product needs next.
Together, the SWOT and the life cycle stage give a picture of the business's position. Marketing decisions later in the process draw on this picture.
draft.remember: Situational analysis asks where the business stands now: SWOT for the whole business, life cycle stage for each product.

a.q: Which item is an internal part of a SWOT analysis?
opts: A skilled team that the business has trained
A new competitor opening across the road
A rise in interest rates across the economy
A shift in customer tastes towards healthier food
a.why: A skilled, trained team is a strength, which is internal and under the business's control. The new competitor is tempting but it is an external threat. Interest rates and customer tastes are also external.
a.clue: Internal means the business can control it.

b.q: Priya's bakery in Orange has a loyal customer base, but a nearby supermarket has just added an in-store bakery. How should these two points be sorted in a SWOT analysis?
opts: Loyal customers a strength, the rival bakery a threat
Loyal customers a strength, the rival bakery a weakness
Loyal customers an opportunity, the rival bakery a threat
Loyal customers an opportunity, the rival bakery a weakness
b.why: Loyal customers belong to the bakery itself, so they are an internal strength. The supermarket bakery is outside the business, so it is an external threat. Calling it a weakness is tempting, but weaknesses are internal.
b.clue: Ask which point sits inside the business and which sits outside it.

a.best: A skilled team that the business has trained

b.best: Loyal customers a strength, the rival bakery a threat
